source.title: DataMan: Data Manager for Pre-training Large Language Models
source.authors: Ru Peng; Kexin Yang; Yawen Zeng; Junyang Lin; Dayiheng Liu; Junbo Zhao

record.file_problem: The main paper and conclusion are present, but the supplied text appears cut off in the appendix, ending during a table.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures the relationship between pretraining perplexity and downstream ICL performance and reports that they are not strictly aligned, qualifying downstream predictability.
record.gate_note: The study does not sweep parameter count, tokens, or compute to fit scaling laws or test compute-optimal allocations. Its relevant result is the reported relationship between perplexity and ICL performance across models trained with different data-selection methods. Other PPL and ICL comparisons are reported in tables, but the task-specific correlation results in Figure 6 are the most direct test of downstream predictability.
record.test_reason: The study correlates SlimPajama validation perplexity with few-shot ICL accuracy across about 37 Sheared-Llama-1.3B models trained on differently selected 30B-token subsets (Figure 6). It argues explicitly that perplexity and ICL are 'not strictly aligned'. This bears on the 'with pretraining loss' half of V6. Loss varies through data selection rather than scale, and there is no scaling sweep or power-law fit, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say PPL and ICL correlate to a degree but are not strictly aligned. They read PPL as reflecting general understanding and ICL as downstream generalization. They attribute the misalignment, most pronounced on LogiQA and MMLU, to domain mismatch and ICL task complexity. The paper's main conclusion is that DataMan-based data selection improves PPL, ICL and instruction following.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies selected pretraining data and measures validation/test perplexity and ICL outcomes; it does not fit scaling laws or search compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The perplexity–ICL association varies by downstream task; the authors particularly identify LogiQA and MMLU as showing misalignment.
record.problems: The scaling-related evidence is limited to Sheared-Llama-1.3B models trained on SlimPajama-derived data; no model-size scaling sweep or scaling-law fit is performed. The reported task correlations have no uncertainty estimates, and the supplied appendix text is truncated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. The paper reports many per-selection perplexity and ICL results in Tables 1 and 12–18, but the task-specific aggregate correlations in Figure 6 directly capture the tested V6 relationship; the study does not test the other claim versions.

untested.parts: Predictability of downstream performance from model scale or compute; only data selection varies at fixed 1.3B size.
No parameter, token or compute sweep, and no power-law fit.
No compute-optimal allocation; Chinchilla is only cited to justify the 30B token budget.
Text pretraining only; the domain continued-pretraining runs report no scaling form.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices compared.

missing.what: Pairwise perplexity–ICL inversions between data-selection variants, which are the basis of the authors' 'not strictly aligned' claim. Overall Score l=4 vs l=5: val PPL 10.21 vs 10.52, avg ICL 47.9 vs 49.1. Sensitivity: PPL 10.11, ICL 48.3. Uniform 45B: PPL 10.09, ICL 46.8.

60B-token runs. Uniform 60B has higher val PPL than uniform 30B (10.81 vs 10.7) yet higher ICL (47.6 vs 44.9). Educational Value 60B has lower PPL than Overall l=5 60B (9.81 vs 9.93) but lower ICL (47.9 vs 50.6).

record.verdict_notes: This is a data-selection paper, not a scaling-law study. Its V6 evidence is cross-model correlation at fixed size (1.3B) and fixed token budget (30B), with loss varied by training data distribution. That is a confounded test of loss-to-downstream predictability, since data mix changes both validation PPL and task-relevant knowledge. Correlations come from figure annotations with no uncertainty, and Pearson is outlier-sensitive. The appendix text is truncated.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep over parameter count, training tokens, or compute; no power-law fits.
No small-run fits or large-run loss predictions.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token growth laws.
No comparison of architecture depth, width, or other details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns text pretraining and does not test other modalities, repeated data, or transfer as a scaling-law setting.
Tests association between pretraining perplexity and downstream ICL performance across data-selection variants, not predictability from model scale.
No fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared across fitting choices or setups.
